question.leadin: Answer some questions about the early colonization of New England.
question.text: This Puritan minister founded Rhode Island after being expelled from Massachusetts. He was one of the first abolitionists and wrote the first book about Native American languages.
question.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

swap.leadin: The split between "Old Lights" and "New Lights" occurred during this period.
swap.text: Evangelists like George Whitfield and Jonathan Edwards were active during what period of intense religious fervor in early colonial America?
swap.clue: A speech from this movement compares its audience to "a spider, or some loathsome insect" held over a fire.

question.leadin: The war saw the British under Anson attacking the Manila Galleon, after which he circumnavigated the globe.
question.text: Identify this war that saw the battles at Porto Bello and Cartagena that was sparked by the Spanish seizure of its namesake's ship, Rebecca.
question.clue: Seeing an unsuccessful amphibious assault on Cartagena de Indias, the incident that sparked this war involved the boarding of the ship Rebecca.

swap.text: Originally intended as a fort to protect the Dutch West India Company's fur interests in the area, this settlement was handed over to the British in exchange for a tiny island near Suriname in the Treaty of Breda. This settlement was later renamed New York City.
swap.clue: A fort in this settlement was constructed by what became a non-Ohio Bowling Green.

question.text: This body was the elected portion of the Virginia General Assembly, the legislative body of colonial Virginia.
question.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

swap.text: This Virginia Governor's policies incited Bacon's Rebellion. This man was appointed by Charles I and replaced Sir Francis Wyatt.
swap.clue: This successor to Francis Wyatt who upset his white constituency by adopting friendlier relations with Native Americans. This governor died before he could explain his actions to King Charles II.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about early leaders in New England.
question.text: This man succeeded John Carver as governor of his colony and detailed its history in Of Plymouth Plantation.
question.clue: His most notable work chronicles the changing of the name of Mount Wallaston to Merry Mountain.

swap.leadin: The author of this work took his pseudonym from the author of Rider's British Merlin, a popular annual collection of facts and figures.
swap.text: Name this work, which, in addition to information about notable dates, included a collection of aphorisms of questionable wisdom such as "Let thy maidservant be faithful, strong and homely."
swap.clue: Naval hero John Paul Jones named his ship after this publication.

question.leadin: The temporary peace achieved under this man's leadership did not last under the rule of his brother Opechancanough (oh-pech-uh n-KAH-noh), who committed the Indian Massacre of 1622.
question.text: Name this Native American weroance, or chief, whose daughter possibly intervened at the last minute to save an Englishman from execution.
question.answerHtml: Powhatan [or Wahunsenacawh; or Powatan; or Pohetan; or Poughwaton; or Wahunsenasawk; or Wahunsenacock; or Wahunsenakah; accept Powhatan Confederacy; prompt on Mamanatowick]
question.clue: He was the high chief among the weorance and held the title of mamanatowick or "emperor" from his capital of Werowocomoco.

swap.leadin: Some historians claim the popularity of the Social Gospel movement as evidence of a third of these events in the 19th century.
swap.text: Name these religious revivals, the second of which was characterized by open air preaching at camp meetings.
swap.clue: This evangelical movement which many have seen as a precursor to the American Revolution.

question.leadin: This colony was the birthplace of Virginia Dare, the first English child born in North America.
question.text: Name this "lost colony" in North Carolina, whose inhabitants disappeared without a trace.
question.clue: After John White returned to England, he was delayed through winter and another three years because of the Spanish Armada and continuing war with Spain.

swap.leadin: Name these players in conflicts between Native Americans and English colonists.
swap.text: This son of Massasoit and ruler of the Wampagnoag lends his name to a 1675 to 1676 war which included the massacre of Narrangaset in the Great Swamp Fight.
swap.clue: He was slain while trying to avoid Benjamin Church's men while hiding in the Miery Swamp near Mount Hope.

question.leadin: Answer the following about King Philip's War.
question.text: This colonial woman was captured by Native Americans during King Philip's War. Her captivity narrative includes the death of her six-year-old daughter, Sarah.
question.clue: During the war, this colonial woman was kidnapped and held for ransom. During her captivity she wrote The Sovereignty and Goodness of God.

swap.text: The Brown family sponsored Esek Hopkins on a disastrous 1764 voyage of a slave ship with this name. A 1998 DNA test supported Annette Gordon-Reed's theory about an enslaved woman with this first name.

question.leadin: This insurrection was spurned by attempts to enforce the Navigation Acts and the Plantation Duty Act.
question.text: Name this insurrection that led to the establishment of a largely independent government for two years in Albemarle County.
question.clue: This 1677 rebellion in the Albemarle region, in which settlers overthrew the colonial government in protest of the enforcement of the Navigation Acts.

swap.leadin: James II tried to consolidate many North American colonies into the Dominion of New England. Name things related to that.
swap.text: This Catholic governor ran the Dominion for most of its existence. His reviled tax and land reforms ended with his ouster, and the Dominion's breakup, right after the Glorious Revolution.
swap.clue: Unpopular measures put forth by this man include Episcopalian worship in the Old South Meetinghouse, strict enforcement of the Navigation Acts, and the suppression of town meetings.

question.text: This President of Harvard spoke out against the Salem witch trials in Cases of Conscience Concerning Evil Spirits. He also penned An Essay for the Recording of Illustrious Provinces, and attacked Edmund Andros in A Narrative of the Miseries of New England.
question.clue: This man became president of Harvard in 1685 and served in that position until 1701.

swap.text: In another work, Miller argues that this man was an artist working in the only medium he could. One work by this man describes "wicked men" who are only useful to God by accident, not design.
swap.clue: This man worked to undo his grandfather Solomon Stoddard's Half-Way Covenant policy, though he inherited Stoddard's land at Northampton.

question.leadin: Name these Indian wars of North America, sadly none of which are the Beaver Wars, FTPE.
question.text: The Battle of Point Pleasant was the culmination of this 1774 war which saw the death of Chief Logan of the Mingo. It's named for John Murray, who commanded colonial forces while serving as governor of Virginia.
question.clue: "Cresap's War," the Yellow Creek Massacre, and the Battle of Point Pleasant were all part of Virginia's efforts against the Shawnee and Mingo in this war, which saw the resistance led by Cornstalk and Chief Logan.

swap.leadin: This conflict was sparked when its namesake was attacked on his ferry on the Susquehanna and was forced to defend himself with oars.
swap.text: Name this colonial conflict of the 1730s, fought over conflicting property disputes in the Susquehanna- Codorus Creek region, which mostly consisted of border raids.
